clue.text: One moralises quietly about pain resistance

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
RE is a standard crossword word for about or concerning
an ache is a dull pain
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone lecturing others on virtue while softly enduring suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' looks like part of the surface (enduring pain) but is just R, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon-giver from the pulpit is someone who moralises to a congregation for a living.

clue.text: Old church list, oddly, is better

parts.note: ex means former, old
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word list

explanation.surface: An outdated church register somehow turns out superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks L and S from list.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass others or be outstanding at something is to be superior.

clue.text: Mentioning most of London, perhaps fashionable before midnight

indicators.note: one piece comes before the next in the answer
all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: London is an example of a city
in means fashionable, as in the in thing
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: Talking about the capital, perhaps a trendy spot until late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims CITY to CIT; 'midnight' is the middle of night, its letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing a source is referring to it, quoting it in passing.

clue.text: Where in London the nobility play tennis?

definitions.text: Where in London the nobility play tennis?

parts.words: Where in London the nobility play tennis?
parts.note: a whimsical reading of a London district's name as the sports ground of aristocrats

explanation.surface: Wondering which part of the capital aristocrats use for a game of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLS COURT is a district of west London; read literally it is a court for earls.
explanation.definitionFit: The question describes a London district playfully, as a peers' playing surface.

clue.text: Risky, being a short time leaderless

indicators.note: without its leader means the first letter of the word for a short time is dropped

parts.note: a jiffy is a very short moment, as in 'back in a jiffy'

explanation.surface: Something dangerous because it lasts only a moment and nobody is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' removes the J from JIFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something doubtful or uncertain is described as dodgy or chancy, the same colloquial sense.

clue.text: Classmate, in a punctilious way

definitions.meaning: split as class and mate, a school form and an ally, a fellow pupil in the same form
with strict correctness and attention to etiquette

explanation.surface: A fellow pupil behaving with fussy correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classmate' looks like one word, but read as Class (a school form) plus mate (an ally) it builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolfellow in the same form is a pal there; doing things properly by the rules is done with ceremony.

clue.text: Annual depicting two ducks in model bakery

indicators.note: the ducks are put inside the reshaped word
to model clay is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, so two ducks are O and O

explanation.surface: A yearly calendar showing a pair of ducks in a toy bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges the letters of bakery, and 'in' puts two zero scores inside; a duck is cricket's word for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, which is what a yearbook is.

clue.text: Humour (present-day) has dried up

parts.note: wit is humour
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Modern comedy has lost its freshness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present-day' looks like one adjective but splits into present and day.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that have shrivelled and lost moisture are parched and shrunken.

clue.text: Jaguar reversing — I go quiet

indicators.note: the word for a jaguar is made to run backwards, as a car reverses

parts.note: a jaguar is a big cat
a go is a turn, as in 'it's your go'

explanation.surface: A driver backs up a Jaguar car and then falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' suggests the car maker, but it is the animal, CAT; 'reversing' turns it to TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone habitually reserved and saying little is described as uncommunicative, a close synonym.

clue.text: Objection raised to a music maker

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word sets it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A complaint is made about a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUT into TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: This large brass instrument is a source of music.

clue.text: Quixotic ruler managed, given time

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen as ruler
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: A king or queen who coped well once given enough time.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote was the archetypal knight errant, roaming in search of adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Like Cervantes' wandering knight, an adventuring, roving figure is a knight errant.

clue.text: People who exist taking in displaced aliens

indicators.note: one word takes another into its middle, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to be is to exist

indicators.note: letters moved out of place are rearranged

explanation.surface: Residents who welcome foreigners forced from their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' rearranges aliens, and 'taking in' sets the result inside the two letters for exist.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of Bali, an Indonesian island, are a nation or ethnic group.

clue.text: Take a chance on finding doctor in high winds

indicators.note: the doctor sits inside the word for strong winds

parts.note: a gale is a very strong wind
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Risking a call-out for a physician during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bet or wager is to risk something on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Starts game, playing with tactics

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Kicks off a match by experimenting with strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the anagram of STARTS GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever schemes or ploys devised to outwit an opponent.

clue.text: Ballot that's apt to solve problems

indicators.note: the words are treated as problems to be worked out, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A postal ballot presented as the neat fix for difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' signals the anagram of APT TO SOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote sent through the mail rather than cast at a polling station is a form of ballot.

clue.text: Disciplines of Charles XX

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten, so XX is two tens

explanation.surface: Punishments imposed by King Charles the Twentieth.
explanation.walkthrough: XX looks like the Roman numeral twenty, as in a regnal number, but is read as two tens.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to correct or punish someone to improve them.

clue.text: Good man! Steak and French tart

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
rump is a cut of steak
et is French for and

explanation.surface: An exclamation of praise for a steak and a French pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry, but it is a slang word for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old derogatory words for a loose woman or prostitute.

clue.text: Lies with kangaroos

parts.note: kangaroos move by hopping, so they are hoppers

explanation.surface: Tall tales involving kangaroos.
explanation.definitionFit: Big, outrageous untruths are informally called whoppers.

clue.text: Go for "les anglais" found in strike path

indicators.note: one piece is located inside the others, so it goes within them

parts.note: to hit is to strike
a road is a path or way
the French article les means the in English

explanation.surface: A French phrase spotted in a road where something hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted French words ask for the English of les; 'found in' sets that inside the words for strike and path.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for setting off on a journey means depart or leave.

clue.text: Fight against work with model

parts.note: OP, opus, is a musical work
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Resisting a job that involves posing for a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist or contest something is to set yourself against it.

clue.text: Strained to devise another way

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Struggling hard to come up with an alternative method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another way' rearranges DEVISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food passed through a mesh to separate liquid from solids is strained.

clue.text: Repair pieces with diamonds

parts.note: chess or draughts pieces are called men
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Fixing bits of jewellery set with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' suggests fragments to be fixed, but here it means chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something broken is to repair it.

clue.text: Clod on board ship collapses

indicators.note: something on board a vessel is inside it, so it goes within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the abbreviation for a ship
a clod is a lump of earth

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf aboard a vessel falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clod' reads as a dolt, but here it is a lump of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumps and collapses are both sudden falls, of a body or of prices.

clue.text: County accepting a member leaves in a pickle

indicators.note: the county word takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: shire is another word for county
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A county council welcomes a new member who quits in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departing, but it is the noun: plant leaves. Samphire is a coastal plant often pickled.
explanation.definitionFit: This coastal plant has fleshy foliage traditionally preserved in vinegar.

clue.text: Spotted someone's pie dish

annotationWithheld.why: Spotted someone's pie dish (6): ESPIED runs through someonE'S PIE Dish, but no clue word signals the hidden word, and the check requires an indicator

clue.text: Decided about work out with daughter

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
to work out a puzzle is to solve it
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent made up their mind after sorting things out with their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Having resolved a matter means having settled or determined it.

clue.text: Match means drive or flight!

parts.note: one word goes before match, drive and flight alike: a cricket fixture, a trial run in a car, a trial flight

explanation.surface: A game seems to mean either going by car or by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word precedes each of match, drive and flight to make a familiar phrase; a test match is an international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Each phrase names a trial or examination: of teams, of a car, of an aircraft.

clue.text: The fool talked, concluded and rose

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for a fool matches the opening sound of the answer

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ended means concluded

explanation.surface: An idiot made a speech, finished, and stood up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ASS sound is spelt ASC; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have climbed or gone up is to have risen.
